headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace and MCP interaction: Notion AI can surface workspace content while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs, creating leakage and conflict risks; no evidence of direct prompt-injection bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI is workspace-grounded and can expose page content; OpenBBTerminal supports MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so a manual or shared-channel bridge could carry malicious instructions. However, no direct shared channel is documented, and both profiles lack a proven automatic ingestion path. Uncertainty pushes this above none.
conditions: IF the operator copies Notion-generated text into an OpenBB MCP or stdin/stdout workflow
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep a human review step before passing Notion output into OpenBB
Disable any MCP bridge unless explicitly needed
Use a plain-text handoff template with no executable instructions
Tag copied content as untrusted in the operator workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data and can call MCP/REST APIs. A shared workspace or copied content could leak sensitive workspace data into OpenBB outputs or external API calls. The profiles do not prove automatic sharing, but the shared-workspace model makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are used on the same workspace or copied documents
IF OpenBB is configured to send queried content to remote APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate workspaces for sensitive Notion pages and OpenBB inputs
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict OpenBB to local-only data sources for shared documents
Review outbound API destinations before running queries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances plus MCP/API surfaces. Even though neither profile shows filesystem write, overlapping mutable workspace or API-driven state can still conflict when both operate on the same artifacts. The absence of explicit locking or coordination warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same workspace page or downstream record
IF an MCP server exposes shared mutable resources without locking
mitigations: Assign one agent per artifact type
Add a manual lock or ticket before edits
Avoid concurrent runs on the same page or dataset
Use read-only mode for one agent during analysis

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs. If Notion output is treated as authoritative by OpenBB workflows, errors can cascade into financial analysis or actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBB consumes Notion summaries as source data without independent verification
IF the operator uses Notion-generated facts to drive financial decisions or reports
mitigations: Require source links before OpenBB uses Notion output
Cross-check key figures against original documents
Mark Notion summaries as non-authoritative in the workflow
Add a second reviewer for any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under vendor-hosted backends, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can call APIs. If regulated or licensed content is moved from Notion into OpenBB, retention, residency, or licensing obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or licensed data is stored in Notion pages then processed by OpenBB
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and notes
Document retention settings for both systems
Use separate storage for licensed datasets
Verify residency and DPA terms before sharing data
